final_candidates.decision_summary: Introducing a negatively charged aspartate into the deeply buried hydrophobic core residue Trp17 causes severe desolvation penalties and disrupts tertiary packing.
Substituting the central beta-strand residue Ile37 with aspartate introduces unfavorable charge into the core and destabilizes the central beta-sheet structure.
Phe40 is critical for stabilizing aromatic packing; introducing a polar acidic residue eliminates hydrophobic stabilization and impairs structural integrity.

stop_reason.detail: Target destabilization objectives are fully addressed by the top-ranked core disrupting candidates.

history.rationale: Trp17 is a highly conserved, bulky aromatic residue packed tightly in the core of the PsaE beta-sandwich fold. Substituting it with a charged Asp residue will severely penalize desolvation and disrupt core packing, driving unfolding.
Introducing a charged aspartate into the deeply buried hydrophobic core residue Trp17 will severely disrupt tertiary packing and destabilize folding.

Ile37 is located within the central hydrophobic beta-strand core. Introducing a negatively charged aspartate into this buried nonpolar environment will cause electrostatic and steric destabilization, disrupting the fold.
Mutation of the central core beta-strand residue Ile37 to an aspartate introduces strong electrostatic repulsion and desolvation penalties.

Phe40 participates in hydrophobic interactions stabilizing the PsaE beta-barrel-like topology. Mutation to an aspartate introduces an uncompensated negative charge into the hydrophobic interior, strongly disrupting folding.
Phe40 participates in essential aromatic core interactions; substituting it with aspartate eliminates hydrophobic stabilization and impairs structural integrity.

Tyr34 is a conserved core-forming aromatic residue essential for stabilizing the antiparallel beta-sheet architecture. Introducing an aspartate destabilizes the tertiary packing through severe desolvation penalties.
Tyr34 forms key hydrophobic and tertiary contacts, so introduction of a negative charge strongly favors uncoupling of the beta-sheet.
Phe48 contributes key hydrophobic contacts between adjacent beta-strands. Mutation to charged aspartate severely compromises structural integrity and promotes protein unfolding.
Phe48 is critical for beta-hairpin stabilization; polar acidic substitution severely penalizes local hydrophobic collapse.
Leu55 is a buried aliphatic residue stabilizing the hydrophobic core near the C-terminal loop/strand region. Mutation to aspartate disrupts hydrophobic cohesion and impairs stable folding.
Leu55 is buried in the C-terminal strand region, and replacement with aspartate disrupts local packing and stability.
Val38 forms part of the hydrophobic beta-sheet interface. Introducing an aspartate causes severe electrostatic repulsion and desolvation penalties within the folded state.
Val38 forms part of the hydrophobic beta-sheet framework, making aspartate incorporation highly destabilizing.
Ile33 is centrally positioned in a beta-strand of PsaE. Mutation to proline will break beta-sheet backbone hydrogen bonding and introduce steric clashes, disrupting the beta-sheet fold.
Proline substitution at Ile33 acts as a powerful beta-sheet breaker, perturbing the main-chain hydrogen bonding network.
Replacing the buried Trp17 with a bulky, positively charged arginine creates severe steric hindrance and buried charge instability in the hydrophobic core.
Placing a bulky, positively charged arginine into the Trp17 core cavity induces severe steric and desolvation penalties.
Phe60 is an aromatic residue involved in C-terminal tertiary contacts. Substitution with an aspartate disrupts the local hydrophobic cluster, destabilizing subunit folding.
Phe60 helps anchor the C-terminal segment into the folded core; replacing it with aspartate hampers native fold stability.
